title: Celery task test depends on external worker/broker
reasoning: The test enqueues the task with add.delay() and then blocks on result.get(timeout=10). Unless the test environment forces Celery eager execution or starts a worker and result backend, this test will time out or fail for infrastructure reasons rather than validating the add task behavior. The declared test command is pytest, so this makes the suite brittle in local/CI runs that only run Django/pytest.
reproduction: Run the test suite without a Celery worker and result backend configured for the test environment; this test will wait for the async result and fail after the timeout instead of executing the task inline.
recommendation: Make the test independent of external Celery infrastructure by calling the task synchronously, e.g. add.run(4, 6) or add(4, 6), or explicitly configure Celery eager mode and an eager result backend in the test settings used by this suite.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is itself a test reliability issue; the current assertion only passes when the surrounding Celery runtime happens to be available or eager mode is configured elsewhere.
suggestedRegressionTest: Keep the add task assertion but execute the task synchronously so the test proves the task logic without requiring a broker or worker.
minimumFixScope: Update tests/tasks/test_add.py or the test settings used by this suite to ensure Celery tasks execute eagerly during tests.
